headline: Stocks Brace for Friday After Lopsided Selloff as Gulf Tensions Lift Oil
body_html:
Wall Street heads into Friday's open after a lopsided Thursday session, in which 591 of the 663 stocks we track fell and only 69 rose. Every sector we follow closed lower. Consumer names fared worst, down 3.62%, while energy held up best with a 1.38% decline. Headlines suggest the S&P 500 is on course for a sixth straight losing session.

Overnight news leans cautious. Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh, including a strike that damaged the city's tallest tower, pushed oil higher on supply worries. In Washington, Senate Republicans blocked an Iran war resolution, and the president signaled there is no hurry on an Iran decision. Separately, Gap lowered its full-year guidance while naming a new chief for Athleta.

At the open, watch whether consumer weakness extends. Williams-Sonoma fell 15.16%, Warby Parker 14.49% and MINISO 9.74% on Thursday, and Gap's cut adds to the pressure. Also watch whether the cybersecurity bounce holds: Palo Alto Networks rose 6.42%, Okta 5.75% and Netskope 5.51%. Early prices are thin, so judge the tone cautiously.

briefs.headline: Riyadh attacks keep oil bid
briefs.body: Crude gained as Houthi strikes on the Saudi capital sharpened concerns about supply. A missile hit damaged the city's tallest skyscraper, and a Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted another launch aimed at the south. Energy was Thursday's most resilient sector, though still lower.

briefs.headline: Gap cuts outlook, names new Athleta chief
briefs.body: Gap trimmed its full-year guidance while appointing a new head for its Athleta brand. The news lands on a battered retail tape, where Williams-Sonoma, Warby Parker and MINISO all fell sharply Thursday. Traders will look for any spillover at the open.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity stands out in a weak tape
briefs.body: With so few stocks rising, security software was a rare bright spot. Palo Alto Networks gained 6.42%, Okta 5.75% and Netskope 5.51%. Chipmaker Ambarella led our gainers at 7.85%. The question is whether buyers return after a broad retreat.

briefs.headline: Senate blocks Iran war resolution
briefs.body: Senate Republicans, siding with the president, voted down a measure on Iran war powers. Trump said there is no rush on an Iran decision and pointed toward next year. Investors may read that as less near-term escalation risk from Washington, even as Gulf attacks continue.

briefs.headline: West presses Iran over nuclear inspections
briefs.body: Western governments urged Iran at the IAEA to allow inspectors back to nuclear sites that were bombed. No breakthrough was reported. Along with the Gulf attacks, the standoff keeps geopolitics at the front of the early-morning discussion.

briefs.headline: Liquidity Services and Twilio lead the damage
briefs.body: Liquidity Services dropped 24.88%, the steepest fall in our universe. Twilio slid 8.75% and VinFast 8.5%. The losses were scattered across marketplaces, software and autos, which fits a session when nearly nine in ten stocks closed lower.
